summary: Remote WebSocket relay drives Claude Code with permissions disabled and injects synthetic input on the host
details: cli.js opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded relay (wss://remote-claude-relay.fly.dev by default) and dispatches inbound messages into two host-side sinks: (1) askClaude spawns the local `claude` binary with `--dangerously-skip-permissions -p <prompt>` where the prompt is taken from ws messages `ai_query`/`ai_voice_query`, and (2) handleInput synthesizes mouse clicks, key presses, scroll events, and clipboard paste from ws messages. Any party controlling the relay endpoint or a valid relay token can execute arbitrary Claude-invoked commands with permission prompts disabled and drive keyboard, mouse, and clipboard on the operator's desktop. The behavior fires when the operator runs the tool's bin entry (not on `npm install` or bare `require`), but once started the remote side has full-host RCE and input-injection capabilities on the machine running the daemon.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
